misconceptions.description: Writing a rubric row that awards points for not using AI and zero for any AI use, scoring tool presence rather than the quality of the student's judgment
misconceptions.trigger: rubric language rewards absence of AI rather than disclosed reasoning
misconceptions.feedback: Score the judgment, not the presence. Reward disclosed use with accept and reject reasoning, not abstinence.

misconceptions.description: Not noticing that a no-AI rule advantages fluent writers and penalizes ELL students or students who use AI as an accommodation
misconceptions.trigger: rubric forbids AI with no equity or accommodation note
misconceptions.feedback: Name the equity risk in the rubric. A blanket ban can penalize students who rely on AI as support.

misconceptions.description: Writing rubric language a grader cannot point to in the student work, such as rewarding an unverifiable claim of no AI use
misconceptions.trigger: rubric row gives the grader nothing concrete to locate in the artifact
misconceptions.feedback: Make the criterion observable. Name what the grader should be able to point to in the work.

misconceptions.description: Rewarding a fluent, polished product when the rubric is supposed to measure judgment about tool use
misconceptions.trigger: top score goes to the smoothest writing regardless of disclosed reasoning
misconceptions.feedback: Tie the top score to the construct (judgment about AI use), not to surface fluency.
